region: DataFeel Dot contact surface — rest-associated profile

loci.basis: NTC thermistor at contact surface. Distal skin temperature rises slightly at sleep onset as core body temperature decreases (Van Someren, 2006). Gentle thermal modulation in this profile targets the 20–37 °C range without active warming above physiological neutral.

Normalised time-of-day (0.0 = midnight, 1.0 = midnight). Rest phase approximately 0.0–0.25 and 0.75–1.0. Host-supplied; not measured by the device. Used as the ABR interior locus (B) with gate inverted: when circadian phase is LOW (biological night), the inverted gate (1−B) is high, and thermal disturbances drive stronger multimodal rest output. This is the complement of the activity profile's gate.

170 Hz resonant actuator. Rest profile uses lower amplitude and longer pulse duration than the activity profile. Low-amplitude vibrotactile stimulation at 170 Hz may support mechanotransduction in superficial tissue without arousal-level sensory activation.

RGB red channel, ~626 nm. The photobiomodulation (PBM) literature documents local tissue effects of 600–700 nm light via cytochrome c oxidase activation, including increased ATP production and anti-inflammatory cytokine modulation (Hamblin, 2016; Karu, 2010). 626 nm is at the lower boundary of this window. This is a local tissue mechanism, distinct from the retinal circadian signalling pathway activated by blue light. Dim output in the rest profile avoids retinal stimulation while remaining within the documented PBM wavelength range.

relations.description: Thermal disturbance (A) drives haptic amplitude (R) gated by inverted circadian phase (1−B). During the rest phase (B low, 1−B high), thermal changes produce a gentler haptic response consistent with the rest profile envelope. Same inverted gate as R-02 — both modalities are simultaneously expressed during the rest phase, producing multimodal resonance in the biological night window.

Thermal disturbance (A) drives red optical output (R) gated by inverted circadian phase (1−B). During the rest phase (B low, 1−B high), thermal changes produce dim red illumination within the PBM wavelength range. The same inverted gate as R-01 means haptic and optical outputs are simultaneously expressed during biological night — the multimodal intersection complementary to the activity profile's daytime resonance window.
